title: Silkworm farming once occupied the attics of Japanese houses
body: In the mountain villages of Shirakawa-go and Gokayama, large houses were built with steep thatched gables. The communities raised silkworms, using the space beneath the roofs for production.
takeaway: Roof space can be a workplace as well as protection from the weather.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Shirakawa-go and Gokayama
visual: a steep thatched roof sheltering a broad timber attic

title: An 1850s railway crossed 41 km of Austrian mountain terrain
body: The Semmering Railway was built between 1848 and 1854. It crossed a mountainous stretch by joining a series of bridges, viaducts and tunnels into a railway that opened up settlements along the route.
takeaway: Rail access changed who could reach mountain districts and encouraged new buildings for visitors.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Semmering Railway (1998)
visual: an old railway curving across a two-storey stone viaduct in the mountains
